summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, who writes embedded C/C++ firmware for ARM Cortex MCUs and RTOS-based robots. Built interrupt-driven, multithreading FreeRTOS firmware with I2C/SPI/UART drivers and PWM actuator control on STM32, plus Python tooling and Linux deployment on Jetson. Comfortable on the bench with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers and multimeters.

Embedded Systems & RTOS: ARM Cortex MCUs (STM32 Cortex-M4, Bare-Metal C)

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers over I2C with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and JupyterHub for collaborative data analysis and technical documentation.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1); achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Built Cortex-M4 firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used multithreading on FreeRTOS (tasks with mutexes) for shared-memory coordination on STM32; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED display.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands and user override.
Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to the STM32 over UART.

projects.name: Robocon Competition Robot — Holonomic Drive & Encoder Odometry
bullets: Implemented interrupt-driven quadrature decoding from first principles (4-bit A/B transition state machine on hardware interrupts) and drove four motor channels at 15 kHz PWM on Arduino Due.
Built closed-loop heading correction from 2400 CPR encoder odometry and a fail-safe state machine that halts all motors on controller disconnect.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via a TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping; resolved 11 integration failures to reach 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials).
Deployed the Jetson arm bridge as a Linux systemd service (auto-restart with backoff, non-root isolation, static IP networking).
